section_summary: This section comprises the concluding portion of the American Embassy in Tokyo's monthly political report for September 1934, Department of State memoranda analyzing Embassy reports, and the beginning of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report for October 1934. Major international matters include the finalized agreement for the sale of the Chinese Eastern Railway to Manchukuo, the British industrial mission under Lord Barnby, Batavia trade parleys, and Japanese diplomatic and naval strategies prior to the 1935 London Naval Conference. Domestic reporting highlights cabinet administrative reforms in Manchuria, civil aviation expansion, military budget battles, and the widespread destruction and budgetary dislocation caused by the Osaka typhoon of September 21, 1934.

subfiles.about: Continuation and conclusion of the American Embassy Tokyo monthly political report for September 1934 reviewing foreign relations, internal politics, finance, economic conditions, and typhoon disaster relief.
subfiles.summary: This concluding section of the Tokyo Embassy's September 1934 monthly report covers the administrative reorganization of Manchukuo into new provinces, the concluded ¥170,000,000 agreement for the purchase of the Chinese Eastern Railway from the Soviet Union, and British-Japanese trade relations fostered by the Federation of British Industries mission. It surveys commercial discussions with British India, the Netherlands Indies, Italy, Germany, and Brazil, alongside border tensions with the USSR and diplomatic interactions with China. On the domestic front, it details military and naval preparations for the 1935 London Naval Conference, disputes over the creation of the Manchurian Bureau, cabinet discussions on agricultural relief, and civil aviation defense planning. The report documents the catastrophe of the September 21 Osaka typhoon and tidal wave, which caused over half a billion yen in damages and prompted plans for an extraordinary Diet session, closing with comprehensive lists of despatches (Nos. 949-991) and telegrams (Nos. 193-216) sent during September.
subfiles.title: Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of September, 1934 (Report No. 96)

subfiles.about: Department of State Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum summarizing and analyzing the Tokyo Embassy's monthly political report for October 1934.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: This memorandum summarizes Embassy Tokyo's Despatch No. 1050 covering Japanese political, diplomatic, and economic developments during October 1934. It highlights Ambassador Hiroshi Saito's return to the United States and his public addresses defending Japanese naval parity claims, Manchukuo diplomacy, and commercial interests in Latin America. The memorandum covers Ambassador William C. Bullitt's transit through Japan, British-Japanese contacts, Dutch-Japanese trade frictions at Batavia, and disputed details in the transfer of the Chinese Eastern Railway. Domestically, it analyzes the centralisation of Japanese administration in Manchuria under the Ambassador at Hsinking, political opposition from the Seiyukai, naval dirigible plans, trials of the reactionary 'God Sent Troops', and the Ministry of Finance's compilation of the 1935-36 budget deficit.
subfiles.title: Tokyo's Political Report for the Month of October (No. 1050, November 19, 1934)

subfiles.about: Department of State Division of Latin-American Affairs memorandum reviewing two newspaper articles on Brazilian foreign exchange restrictions.
subfiles.from: Division of Latin-American Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: This concise departmental memorandum assesses two enclosed newspaper clippings addressing the debate over Brazilian exchange regulations. It advises that reading the entire text of the articles is unnecessary, highlighting only their core divergence. It notes that the subsidized article by Freites advocates the renewal of exchange restrictions, whereas the article by Bouças cites Professor George F. Warren in arguing that exchange control cannot be dismantled under existing economic circumstances.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Regarding Newspaper Articles on Brazilian Exchange Restrictions

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmitting Embassy Tokyo's monthly report on political and economic conditions in Japan for October 1934.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits Report No. 97 on conditions in Japan during October 1934, forwarding copies to the Department and to American diplomatic and consular posts across China and Manchuria. The enclosed report contains an exhaustive table of contents and opens with a thorough treatment of United States-Japanese relations. It reviews Ambassador Hiroshi Saito's return to the United States, his public speeches denouncing the Washington and London naval treaty ratios, and an eight-point policy program agreed with senior Tokyo officials upholding the Hull-Hirota notes while insisting on an independent line in East Asia and opposing the Stimson Doctrine. The report also details the Tokyo visit of Ambassador William C. Bullitt and exposes a fabricated interview published by the Tokyo Nichi Nichi.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1050: Report on Conditions in Japan for the Month of October, 1934 (Enclosing Report No. 97)
